prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: automated hospital medication dispensing/returns; goals timeliness, pharmacist oversight, traceability. Aliases: Medication Order Gateway=Morrowglass; Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot=Cinderwake; Pharmacy Verification Station=Juniper; Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler=Bluejay; Medication Return Kiosk=Tallowmere; Registered Nurse=Larkspur; Pharmacy Technician=Copperfield; Biomedical Engineer=Stonewake. Elements: Medication Order Gateway accepts orders from authorized clinical systems, records arrival, validates fields/patient IDs/codes/quantities/destinations, flags missing/duplicate/conflicting data, routes to pharmacy review, sends status, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Pharmacy Verification Station shows queue/validation, final verification before release, audit record. Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot prepares only authorized orders, records handling, produces Priority Refill Tote Tag. Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler keeps stock in range, records temps, reports excursions/connectivity loss. East and West Tube Dispatch Consoles route deliveries via Pneumatic Tube Network; East console monitors capsules, records route/timing/equipment status, sends Tube Route Exception Ticket on route deviation or delivery timeout. North and South Ward Cabinet Controllers report availability, block dispensing when Out of Service. Medication Return Kiosk records returns, produces Return Bin Audit Label. Actors: Clinical Pharmacist approves orders, judges suitability of stock affected by storage/delivery timing, produces Dose Exception Review Slip. Pharmacy Technician preps, investigates discrepancies, checks cooler stock, verifies capsule contents/IDs before redelivery, produces Cold Chain Handoff Card. Medication Safety Officer reviews trends, produces Diversion Review Packet. Registered Nurse confirms ongoing need, follows contingency. Charge Nurse informs staff of delays, sends Cabinet Downtime Notice, confirms notification before cabinet restore. Hospital Courier manual transport. Biomedical Engineer inspects tube hardware/switches/sensors and cabinet hardware, verifies after repair. IT Operations Specialist checks console/controller connectivity, interfaces, logs. Dispatch personnel hold capsules, block faulty routes; operations staff coordinate alternate routes, authorize route return. Technical staff document fault/corrective action/verification in service record. Rules: unresolved discrepancies block preparation; no dispensing until checks/authorization; excursion stock and returns segregated pending disposition; tube segment unavailable until tested safe; dispatch resumes only after checks and operations authorization; cabinet downtime is controlled interruption preserving accountability via authorized alternative location. Modes: normal automated routing; manual courier fallback; route fault/alternate route; cabinet Out of Service contingency.

New part:
S072: A cabinet remains unavailable until its controller reports Ready for Dispense and required operational checks are complete.
S073: Operations closes the interruption only after staff confirm that dispensing and delivery workflows are functioning as intended.
S074: Final pharmacy release occurs only after the order, prepared medication, and intended destination have been checked against the approved dispensing instructions.
S075: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews clinical and labeling exceptions that require professional judgment before authorizing release.
S076: The Pharmacy Technician confirms that the package contents and patient identifiers match the verified order.
S077: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot presents the completed package at the Pharmacy Verification Station for the final check.
S078: The Pharmacy Verification Station records the verification outcome and prevents release while required checks remain incomplete.
S079: The Pharmacy Verification Station produces the Batch Release Note after the final release checks are recorded.
S080: The release decision is associated with the order identifier, package identifier, verification time, and responsible staff credentials.
S081: The Medication Order Gateway provides the current order status used to confirm that the request remains valid.
S082: A canceled, duplicated, or superseded request is held for resolution rather than placed into a delivery load.
S083: The Clinical Pharmacist documents the disposition of any clinical concern before the package can proceed.
S084: Supporting records are prepared before a load enters the delivery network so staff can establish what was released and under which conditions.
S085: The load manifest identifies each package, its intended destination, handling requirements, and the time it was assembled.
S086: Package identifiers are checked against the manifest to detect omissions, substitutions, or duplicate entries.
S087: Temperature-sensitive packages remain under controlled conditions until their custody is formally transferred.
S088: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler records temperature conditions while medication awaits transfer.
S089: At the physical handoff, the Hospital Courier checks package count, packaging integrity, destination information, and any special handling instructions.
S090: The courier records the time and identity associated with acceptance so the custody history remains traceable.
S091: The Hospital Courier produces the Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record when the capsule is sealed for transfer.
S092: The courier verifies that the capsule is closed securely and that its contents are not exposed during handling.
S093: The Pneumatic Tube Network accepts only loads that meet the applicable packaging and routing requirements.
S094: The East Tube Dispatch Console checks the requested route and reports whether the route is available for dispatch.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
